
# base

Schemaless, transactional document database with a CouchDB-shaped HTTP API.
SQLite underneath: `rusqlite` natively, D1 on Cloudflare Workers.

- JSON documents, per-document integer revisions (`_rev`).
- Mango queries (`_find`) with optional indexes.
- Multi-document, multi-database transactions (`/_txn`) using optimistic concurrency.
- Change feed (`_changes`) ordered by a global `seq`.
- Bearer-token auth with `read`, `write`, `admin` roles, optionally scoped to databases.

## Pages

| page | covers |
|---|---|
| [Getting started](getting-started) | run locally, deploy to Cloudflare, first requests |
| [npm package](npm) | typed SDK and HTTP-shaped handler for Node, Bun, Deno, browsers, Workers: `npm i @egig/base` |
| [HTTP API](api) | every endpoint, request and response shapes, errors |
| [Queries](queries) | `_all_docs`, Mango `_find`, indexes, `_changes` |
| [Transactions](transactions) | `/_txn`, reads, guards, conflicts |
| [Auth and limits](auth-and-limits) | keys, roles, limits, naming rules |

## For LLMs and agents

- [llms.txt](llms.txt): short index.
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): all documentation in one plain-text file.



# Getting started

No Rust? Use the [npm package](npm) instead: `npm i @egig/base`.

## Run natively

```sh
BASE_KEYS='[{"key":"devkey-12345","access":"admin"}]' cargo run -p base-server
# or, no auth (everyone is admin; local development only):
cargo run -p base-server -- --no-auth
```

Server options:

| flag | env | default |
|---|---|---|
| `--db` | `BASE_DB` | `base.db` (SQLite file) |
| `--listen` | `BASE_LISTEN` | `127.0.0.1:5984` |
| `--keys` | `BASE_KEYS` | none (every request is 401) |
| `--no-auth` | | off |

## Run on Cloudflare Workers

Needs `cargo install worker-build` and `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

```sh
cd crates/worker
npx wrangler dev          # keys come from .dev.vars
```

Deploy:

```sh
npx wrangler d1 create base            # put the id in wrangler.toml
npx wrangler secret put BASE_KEYS
npx wrangler deploy
```

`.dev.vars` example:

```
BASE_KEYS=[{"key":"devkey-12345","access":"admin"}]
```

## First requests

```sh
H='Authorization: Bearer devkey-12345'
B=http://127.0.0.1:5984

curl -X PUT  $B/notes -H "$H"                                  # {"ok":true}
curl -X PUT  $B/notes/n1 -H "$H" -d '{"title":"hi","n":1}'     # {"ok":true,"id":"n1","rev":"1"}
curl         $B/notes/n1 -H "$H"                               # {"_id":"n1","_rev":"1","title":"hi","n":1}
curl -X PUT  $B/notes/n1 -H "$H" -d '{"_rev":"1","title":"hello","n":2}'   # rev "2"
curl -X POST $B/notes/_find -H "$H" -d '{"selector":{"n":{"$gte":1}}}'
curl -X DELETE "$B/notes/n1?rev=2" -H "$H"
```

## Admin page

`GET /_ui` serves a static admin page. It is public and holds no data; it sends your token with each API call.
`GET /` is also public and returns `{"name":"base","version":"..."}`.



# npm package

`@egig/base` runs the database inside your own process. The engine ships as prebuilt WebAssembly, so you do not clone the repo or install Rust. You supply the SQLite or D1 handle. The HTTP API is the same as the server's: see [HTTP API](api).

```sh
npm i @egig/base
```

## Node (22.5 or newer)

```ts
import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";
import { createBase } from "@egig/base";
import { sqliteStore } from "@egig/base/stores/sqlite";

const db = await createBase({
  store: sqliteStore(new DatabaseSync("app.db")),
  keys: [{ key: "devkey-12345", access: "admin" }],
});

const headers = { authorization: "Bearer devkey-12345", "content-type": "application/json" };
await db.fetch(new Request("http://x/notes", { method: "PUT", headers }));
const res = await db.fetch(
  new Request("http://x/notes/a", { method: "PUT", headers, body: JSON.stringify({ title: "hi" }) }),
);
console.log(await res.json()); // { ok: true, id: "a", rev: "1" }
```

The host in the URL is ignored; only the path and query matter.

`sqliteStore` accepts a `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync`, a `better-sqlite3` database, or a `bun:sqlite` `Database`.

## SDK (no HTTP)

`openBase` skips Request/Response and gives typed methods. The path is TS, then SDK, then the wasm engine, then SQLite. The SDK is trusted: there are no keys and everything is admin.

```ts
import { openFile } from "@egig/base/node";

const base = await openFile("app.db"); // sets WAL and a 5 s busy timeout
const notes = await base.createDb<{ title: string; n: number }>("notes");

const { rev } = await notes.put("a", { title: "hi", n: 1 });   // create-only: throws a conflict if "a" exists
await notes.put("a", { title: "hello", n: 2 }, { rev });       // update from rev
await notes.get("a");                                          // { _id, _rev, title, n } or null
await notes.update("a", (d) => ({ ...d!, n: d!.n + 1 }));      // read-modify-write, retries on conflict
await notes.createIndex(["n"]);
const { docs } = await notes.find({ selector: { n: { $gte: 1 } }, sort: [{ n: "desc" }], limit: 10 });
await notes.delete("a", (await notes.get("a"))!._rev);
base.close();
```

With your own store (Workers, Bun, better-sqlite3) use `openBase({ store })` from `@egig/base` or `@egig/base/workers`.

| method | notes |
|---|---|
| `base.createDb(name)` | returns the handle; fine if it exists |
| `base.db(name)` | handle, does not create |
| `base.dropDb(name)`, `base.listDbs()` | |
| `base.txn({ reads?, guards?, ops })` | see [Transactions](transactions) |
| `base.raw` | the `fetch`/`handle` object, auth off. Do not expose it publicly |
| `db.get(id)` | doc or `null` |
| `db.put(id, doc, { rev? })` | no `rev` = create only |
| `db.post(doc)` | generated id |
| `db.delete(id, rev)` | |
| `db.update(id, fn, retries = 5)` | return `undefined` from `fn` to skip the write |
| `db.find({ selector, sort?, limit?, skip? })` | see [Queries](queries) |
| `db.allDocs({ startkey?, endkey?, limit?, skip?, descending?, includeDocs? })` | |
| `db.changes({ since?, limit?, includeDocs? })` | |
| `db.info()` | |
| `db.createIndex(fields, name?)`, `db.indexes()`, `db.dropIndex(name)` | |

Failures throw `BaseError` with `status`, `error`, `reason` (the same as the [HTTP errors](api)) and `isConflict`. `get` returns `null` instead of throwing on 404.

## Serve over HTTP

`db.fetch` has the standard `(Request) => Promise<Response>` shape.

```ts
Bun.serve({ port: 5984, fetch: (req) => db.fetch(req) });
Deno.serve({ port: 5984 }, (req) => db.fetch(req));
```

On Node, use any Request/Response adapter, for example `@hono/node-server`.

## Cloudflare Workers (D1)

```ts
import { createBase, d1Store } from "@egig/base/workers";

let db: ReturnType<typeof createBase> | undefined;

export default {
  fetch(req: Request, env: { DB: D1Database; BASE_KEYS: string }) {
    db ??= createBase({ store: d1Store(env.DB), keys: JSON.parse(env.BASE_KEYS) });
    return db.then((b) => b.fetch(req));
  },
};
```

Use the `@egig/base/workers` entry. It imports the `.wasm` as a module, which wrangler bundles; Workers cannot compile wasm from bytes at runtime. The schema is applied on first use.

Set the keys with `npx wrangler secret put BASE_KEYS`. Add a D1 binding named `DB` in `wrangler.toml`.

## Browser

Pass any `Store` (for example one over sql.js or wa-sqlite). The wasm loads from `import.meta.url`. If your bundler moves the file, pass it yourself:

```ts
import wasmUrl from "@egig/base/base.wasm?url"; // Vite
await createBase({ store, noAuth: true, wasm: wasmUrl });
```

## Options

| option | meaning |
|---|---|
| `store` | required. Where data lives. |
| `keys` | array of `{ key, access, dbs? }`. Same meaning as `BASE_KEYS`: see [Auth and limits](auth-and-limits). |
| `noAuth` | `true` makes everyone admin. Local development only. Pass `keys` or `noAuth`; `createBase` throws if you pass neither. |
| `wasm` | `WebAssembly.Module`, bytes, `Response`, or URL. Default: the file shipped in the package. |

`createBase` returns `{ fetch(Request), handle({ method, path, query?, bearer?, body? }) }`. `path` is percent-encoded. `handle` returns `{ status, contentType, body: Uint8Array }`.

## Custom store

```ts
interface Store {
  batch(stmts: { sql: string; params: (string | number | null)[] }[]): Promise<(string | number | null)[][][]>;
}
```

Rules:

- Run all statements in order inside one atomic transaction.
- Return, per statement, its rows as arrays of column values (`[]` if none).
- If any statement fails, roll back the whole batch and throw. Do not change the error message: a failed transaction guard is detected from it and becomes a 409.

## Notes

- One process, one writer. If several processes share one SQLite file, each batch still runs in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, but set a busy timeout on your handle.
- `createBase` applies the schema on every call. It is idempotent, so restarts are safe.



# HTTP API

All bodies are JSON. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on every request except `GET /` and `GET /_ui`.

## Endpoints

| method and path | access | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /` | none | `{"name":"base","version":"0.1.0"}` |
| `GET /_ui` | none | admin page (HTML) |
| `GET /_all_dbs` | read | array of db names the key can read |
| `PUT /{db}` | admin | create db. 201 `{"ok":true}`. 412 `file_exists` if present |
| `GET /{db}` | read | `{"db_name","doc_count","update_seq"}` |
| `DELETE /{db}` | admin | delete db with all docs and indexes. 200 `{"ok":true}` |
| `POST /{db}` | write | create doc with generated id (or `_id` in body). 201 |
| `GET /{db}/{id}` | read | the doc, with `_id` and `_rev` |
| `PUT /{db}/{id}` | write | create or update. 201 `{"ok":true,"id","rev"}` |
| `DELETE /{db}/{id}?rev=N` | write | delete. 200 `{"ok":true,"id","rev"}`. Leaves a tombstone |
| `GET /{db}/_all_docs` | read | see [Queries](queries) |
| `POST /{db}/_find` | read | see [Queries](queries) |
| `GET /{db}/_changes` | read | see [Queries](queries) |
| `GET /{db}/_index` | read | list indexes |
| `POST /{db}/_index` | admin | create index |
| `DELETE /{db}/_index/{name}` | admin | drop index |
| `POST /_txn` | write | see [Transactions](transactions) |

Wrong method on a known path: 405 `method_not_allowed`. Unknown `/{db}/_name`: 404.

## Documents

A document is a JSON object. `_id` and `_rev` are managed by base:

- `_rev` is a per-document integer rendered as a string (`"1"`, `"2"`, ...). Only the latest revision is stored.
- `PUT` without a `_rev` is create-only. If the doc exists, you get 409.
- Update with `_rev` in the body or `?rev=` in the query. `?rev=` wins if both are given. A stale `_rev` gives 409.
- `_id` in a `PUT` body must equal the path id.
- Other top-level fields starting with `_` are rejected.
- Deleting a doc then `PUT`ting it again without `_rev` re-creates it. `GET` of a deleted doc is 404 with reason `deleted`; a never-existing doc is 404 `missing`.

```sh
curl -X PUT $B/notes/n1 -d '{"title":"a"}'                      # 201 {"ok":true,"id":"n1","rev":"1"}
curl -X PUT $B/notes/n1 -d '{"title":"b"}'                      # 409 conflict
curl -X PUT "$B/notes/n1?rev=1" -d '{"title":"b"}'              # 201 rev "2"
curl -X POST $B/notes -d '{"title":"auto id"}'                  # 201 {"ok":true,"id":"<generated>","rev":"1"}
```

## Errors

Every error is `{"error":"<name>","reason":"<text>"}`.

| status | error | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `bad_request` | invalid JSON, name, id, selector, or parameter |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | missing or unknown bearer token |
| 403 | `forbidden` | key lacks the role or db scope |
| 404 | `not_found` | db, doc, index, or endpoint missing |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` | |
| 409 | `conflict` | stale or missing `_rev`, create over existing doc, failed guard, or index name clash |
| 412 | `file_exists` | database already exists |
| 413 | `too_large` | body over 2,000,000 bytes |
| 500 | `internal_error` | details are not exposed |



# Queries

## `GET /{db}/_all_docs`

Query parameters (plain strings, not JSON-encoded):

| param | default | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `startkey` / `start_key` | | inclusive lower bound on id |
| `endkey` / `end_key` | | inclusive upper bound on id |
| `limit` | 25 | max 1000 |
| `skip` | 0 | |
| `descending` | false | |
| `include_docs` | false | adds `doc` to each row |

```json
{"offset":0,"rows":[{"id":"n1","key":"n1","value":{"rev":"1"},"doc":{"_id":"n1","_rev":"1"}}],"update_seq":7}
```

Deleted docs are not listed.

## `POST /{db}/_find` (Mango)

```json
{"selector":{"age":{"$gte":18},"addr":{"city":"Oslo"}},
 "sort":["age",{"name":"desc"}],
 "limit":10,"skip":0}
```

Response:

```json
{"docs":[{"_id":"...","_rev":"1","age":20}],"update_seq":7,"warning":"No matching index found, falling back to a scan of the database."}
```

- `selector` is required. `limit` defaults to 25, max 1000.
- Results are ordered by `sort`, then by `id`. No `sort` = by id.
- Field names are dotted paths of `[A-Za-z0-9_]` segments, e.g. `addr.city`. A plain nested object is a subfield match.
- Operators: implicit `$eq`, `$eq $ne $gt $gte $lt $lte $in $nin $exists`, and `$and $or $nor $not`.
- `warning` appears when no index covers the selector: the query scans the whole db.
- `update_seq` can be used as a `db` guard in a [transaction](transactions) to protect against phantom reads.

## Indexes

```sh
curl -X POST $B/notes/_index -d '{"fields":["age"],"name":"by_age"}'   # 201 {"result":"created","name":"by_age"}
curl $B/notes/_index                                                    # {"indexes":[{"name":"by_age","fields":["age"]}]}
curl -X DELETE $B/notes/_index/by_age                                   # {"ok":true}
```

- `fields`: 1 to 8 dotted paths. `name` optional (default: fields joined with `_`); `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, max 64.
- Same name and same fields again: 200 `{"result":"exists"}`. Same name, different fields: 409.
- A query is covered when its first index field appears in the selector.
- Index creation on a large db is slow on D1.

## `GET /{db}/_changes`

| param | default | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `since` | 0 | return changes with `seq` greater than this |
| `limit` | 100 | max 1000 |
| `include_docs` | false | |

```json
{"results":[{"seq":5,"id":"n1","changes":[{"rev":"2"}],"doc":{"_id":"n1","_rev":"2"}},
            {"seq":6,"id":"n2","changes":[{"rev":"3"}],"deleted":true}],
 "last_seq":6}
```

- Latest state per doc only (not a history), ordered by `seq` then id.
- Deleted docs appear with `"deleted":true` and no `doc`.
- A transaction stamps all its writes with one `seq`; a page is never split in the middle of one `seq`, so it can exceed `limit`.
- Poll with `since=<last_seq>`. No long-poll or SSE yet.



# Transactions

D1 has no interactive transactions, so base uses optimistic concurrency. You send reads you depended on, guards, and writes in one request. base validates and applies them in one atomic batch.

```jsonc
POST /_txn
{
  "reads":  [{"db":"acct","id":"a","rev":"1"}, {"db":"acct","id":"new"}],  // rev omitted = must be absent
  "guards": [{"kind":"db","db":"acct","seq":42}],   // fail if anything in db changed after seq 42
  "ops": [
    {"op":"put","db":"acct","id":"a","rev":"1","doc":{"bal":50}},          // rev omitted = create only
    {"op":"delete","db":"acct","id":"b","rev":"3"}
  ]
}
// 200 {"ok":true,"seq":43,"results":[{"db":"acct","id":"a","rev":"2"}, ...]}
// 409 on any stale rev or failed guard; nothing applied
```

Fields (all arrays optional):

- `reads`: `{db, id, rev?}`. The doc must be at `rev`, or absent/deleted when `rev` is omitted. Checked per document.
- `guards`: `{"kind":"db","db","seq"}`. Fails if any doc in `db` was written after `seq`. Use the `update_seq` returned by `_find` or `_all_docs` to protect a query result from phantoms.
- `ops`: `put` (`rev` omitted = create only, else update from `rev`) and `delete` (`rev` required).

Rules:

- Max 50 ops, 100 reads, 20 guards. 1 MB per doc.
- One op per document per transaction (duplicates are 400).
- Writes need `write` on every db touched; reads and guards need `read`.
- All writes share one global `seq`, returned as `seq`. `results` has one entry per op, in order.
- Missing db: 404, nothing applied.

## Retry pattern

1. `GET` the docs, remember each `_rev`.
2. Compute new values.
3. `POST /_txn` with those revs in `ops` (and `reads` for docs you only read).
4. On 409, go to step 1.

## Cloudflare Free plan

Free caps D1 queries per Worker invocation at 50. Each op costs about 3 statements, so large transactions need the Paid plan.



# Auth and limits

## Keys

Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys come from `BASE_KEYS`, a JSON array:

```json
[{"key":"admin-key-1234","access":"admin"},
 {"key":"app-key-12345","access":"write","dbs":["notes"]},
 {"key":"ro-key-12345","access":"read","dbs":["*"]}]
```

- `key`: 8 or more characters.
- `access`: `read` < `write` < `admin`. Higher roles include lower ones.
- `dbs`: databases the key may touch. Omitted or containing `"*"` = all.
- No keys configured = every request is 401 (except `GET /` and `GET /_ui`).
- Key comparison is constant-time.

| role | can |
|---|---|
| `read` | `GET` docs, `_all_docs`, `_find`, `_changes`, `_index` (list), db info, `_all_dbs` |
| `write` | read, plus create/update/delete docs, `/_txn` |
| `admin` | write, plus create/delete databases, create/delete indexes |

A key outside its role or `dbs` scope gets 403. `_all_dbs` only lists dbs the key can read.

## Naming rules

- Database: `[a-z0-9_-]`, 1 to 64 chars, must not start with `_` or `-`.
- Document id: 1 to 256 chars, no control characters, must not start with `_`.
- Index name: `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, max 64.
- Field path (indexes, selectors, sort): dotted segments of `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, max 128.
- Top-level doc fields starting with `_` are reserved (`_id`, `_rev` only).

## Limits

| | |
|---|---|
| request body | 2,000,000 bytes |
| document | 1,000,000 bytes |
| ops / reads / guards per `/_txn` | 50 / 100 / 20 |
| `limit` on `_all_docs`, `_find` | max 1000 (default 25) |
| `limit` on `_changes` | max 1000 (default 100) |
| index fields | 1 to 8 |

## Known limits

- Only the latest revision of a doc is stored. Deletes leave tombstones; no compaction yet.
- `_find` without an index scans the whole db.
- `DELETE /{db}` on a very large db may exceed D1 per-request limits.
- Queries inside a `/_txn` are not re-run at commit; use `db` guards.
- No long-poll `_changes`, attachments, or replication.
